answer: One defense is anchored commitment with delayed reveal. Each new agent must publish a hash of its identity kernel to a public randomness beacon several epochs before it may transact, posting a small deposit per commitment; the beacon later selects which commitments must be revealed and audited. An attacker spinning up thousands of identities has to pre-commit every one, lock a deposit on each, and gamble that none is drawn, since a failed audit burns the whole batch. Like a sonnet, the rigid form is the point: cost grows with every fake, while an honest agent pays once.
